A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cytobrush sampling alters genital immune parameters at short time points, but only antigen presenting cell number increases persist at 48 h.
the cytobrush sampling procedure has an impact on cervico-vagal immune parameters and microbial composition, but that these effects are relatively transient.

The main takeaway from our work is that
cervical cytobrush collection is associated with significant changes in endocervical cell numbers and cytokine levels, and these changes persist for up to 48 hours after sampling.
the collection of endocervial cells by a cervical cytobrush can alter the immunological profile of the female genital mucosa for at least 48 hours.

the use of cytobrush sampling for longitudinal assessment of the endocervical mucosal immune system is associated with significant alterations to the endocervix, which should be taken into consideration when assessing the impact of HIV risk factors and/or interventions on genital immune function.
